A Response Envelope

Every success response wraps its payload the same way — data alone, or data plus meta.

So far, a successful response has just been res.json(ticket) or res.json(tickets) — whatever shape the service happened to return, sent straight to the client. That's fine with one resource. It stops being fine once Comment and Tag land in this lesson too, each with their own list and single-item responses: nothing guarantees GET /tickets, GET /tickets/:id/comments, and GET /tags shape their JSON the same way, unless something enforces it.

The fix is a small, fixed envelope every success response goes through, defined once:

// Figure 3.1: the response envelope (src/utils/response.js)
export const sendResource = (res, data, status = 200) => res.status(status).json({ data });

export const sendCollection = (res, data, meta) =>
  res.status(200).json(meta ? { data, meta } : { data });

A single resource — one ticket, one comment — always arrives as { "data": { ... } }. A list always arrives as { "data": [...] }, with an optional meta key alongside it for anything about the list itself rather than its items — pagination info, added later this lesson, is the only thing that uses it so far. sendResource also takes an optional status, so the same helper covers both 200 OK (fetching/updating something) and 201 Created (making something new) without needing two functions.

This is two plain functions, not a Resource/Transformer class a controller would extend or instantiate (see CLAUDE.md) — it doesn't describe what fields a ticket has, only the envelope every response sits inside, which is a much smaller job.
